articles.title: Semantic Observability for Autonomous Systems Diagnostics
articles.content: Modern distributed microservice deployments generate massive volumes of heterogeneous, multi-format observability logs across physically and logically partitioned infrastructure. Isolating root causes during cascading failures remains an arduous task for Site Reliability Engineers (SREs), bottlenecked by manual keyword filtering and disjointed temporal correlation across monitoring dashboards. We introduce Semantic Observability, an autonomous multi-agent framework that unifies disparate log streams into a dynamic, queryable Property Graph Database. By modeling physical infrastructure topologies, logical software dependencies, and chronological event sequences as attributed nodes and directed relations, it bridges the semantic gap inherent in flat, unstructured log repositories. Building on this unified substrate, we deploy a stateful multi-agent system orchestrated through Directed Cyclic Graphs (DCGs). The system autonomously navigates the topology, applying causal graph algorithms and temporal back-traversal to isolate the precise blast radius of anomalies. The pruned subgraph is then interpreted by a Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning engine to generate contextualized, code-level Root Cause Analyses (RCA) and actionable remediations. This paper establishes the foundational system architecture, formal relational ontology, and multi-agent control loops of Semantic Observability. We show conceptually how the framework eliminates ambient telemetry noise, reduces Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR), compresses LLM token consumption, and prevents structural hallucinations. We also specify an open-source validation framework on standard benchmarks (LogHub and Train-Ticket), laying the groundwork for a forthcoming companion paper on exhaustive quantitative evaluation and production benchmarking.

articles.title: Benchmarking Arabic Dialects for Math Problems
articles.content: Mathematical reasoning remains underexplored for low-resource languages, including Dialectal Arabic. To bridge this gap, we introduce the DAR-MGSM (Dialectal Arabic Multilingual Grade School Math) Benchmark, the first manually curated benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning in Dialectal Arabic. DAR-MGSM consists of math word problems (MWPs) requiring multi-step reasoning and covers five major Arabic dialects alongside Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). The benchmark comprises two parallel versions: translated-only and translated & culturally localized. The latter version adapts entities and references to regional varieties. We evaluate eleven Arabic-centric and multilingual large language models on DAR-MGSM. The results show that the performance generally declines on the localized version, highlighting the challenges introduced by culturally grounded adaptations. However, the magnitude of this effect varies across models, with Arabic-centric models exhibiting different levels of sensitivity to localization. A mechanistic interpretability analysis shows that translated and localized variants of the same MWPs often induce distinct internal reasoning trajectories, even when aggregate accuracy remains similar. Overall, our results show that mathematical reasoning performance depends on both linguistic variety and cultural context.

articles.title: Value-Rich, Differently Organized: Measuring Value Expression and Organization in AI-Generated Debates
articles.content: Current evaluation of LLM-generated debate largely focuses on argumentative quality, leaving the value structure of generated arguments underexamined. We introduce a diagnostic metric framework for comparing how values are expressed and organized in human-reference and AI-generated debates. The framework separates value expression, the range of recognizable values a debate invokes, from value organization, how those values are distributed and sustained across turns. Grounded in Schwartz's Basic-10 value theory, it represents debates as multi-level value distributions over argumentative units, utterances, stances, and full debates, enabling metrics for value coverage, alignment, diffusion, and cross-turn dynamics. Across multiple generation systems, AI-generated debates are broadly value-expressive, often activating as many or more value dimensions than matched human references, but they organize these values differently. Their utterances are more locally value-diffuse, and source-blind judges distinguish value clarity from value focus. These findings show that debate evaluation should consider not only value presence, but also value organization. Code and supplementary materials are available at https://github.com/Maoyuan-li/Value-Expression-and-Organization.

articles.title: Turning TS2Vec into a Foundation Model for Time Series Classification
articles.content: TS2Vec is one of the strongest self-supervised methods for time series classification, introduced in 2022. It is designed to be trained anew on every dataset: self-supervised pre-training followed by linear probing. Since then, the field has shifted towards foundation models that reuse one encoder across datasets. Yet TS2Vec offers a compact convolutional architecture that operates directly on temporal samples and accepts variable-length inputs without resampling. We ask whether these properties can be retained when the encoder is pre-trained only once, and show that they can: TS2Vec can essentially be turned into a foundation model. Three changes suffice: pre-train on a synthetic corpus, feed the encoder a raw amplitude view and an instance-normalized shape view of the input through two small stems, and distill one specialist encoder per view into a single encoder. The result, TS2Vec-FM, is a 1.6M-parameter dilated convolutional network that, kept frozen, reaches 83.3% on UCR-128 and 75.3% on UEA-27 under linear probing, within 0.3 pp of MantisV2, the current state of the art, and above TS2Vec trained separately on each target dataset. What we find most interesting is how different TS2Vec-FM is from other foundation models in design: near-parity is reached without attention, without a patch tokenizer, and without intermediate-layer extraction, using an "old-school" convolutional encoder and a two-layer MLP stem.

articles.title: Evolving Agent Interfaces
articles.content: Computer-use agents are limited by the interfaces humans give them. An agent may type a spreadsheet cell by cell when a single line of code would do, or print all two thousand lines of a file through a shell to find one function. Both the interfaces and the knowledge of when to use each are built by hand, which cannot keep pace with new applications, workflows, and models. We argue that interface design should itself be an agent capability. We introduce Agent S4, an autonomous computer-use scientist that builds Evolving Agent Interfaces from task experience. A meta-agent examines task agents' trajectories on synthetic training tasks, without success labels, and constructs and revises interfaces and usage knowledge in a repository. Population-based evolution then selects which repositories to develop further by their performance on validation tasks the meta-agent never sees, favoring changes that generalize beyond the seen tasks. On OSWorld V2, Agent S4, with Qwen3.8-27B and the evolved repository of interfaces, sets a new state of the art in open-source computer-use agents, reaching 21.3% binary score, 3.8 times the same model with fixed interfaces. This is above both GPT-5.5 (13.0%) and Claude Opus 4.8 (20.6%), at about 4.3% and 1.5% of their respective costs. On ScienceBoard, the evolved interfaces improve the success rate from 41.4% to 58.6% with the same model. These results suggest that useful interfaces can be evolved from experience, making autonomous interface design a source of improvement complementary to advances in models and harnesses. We open-source our code at https://github.com/simular-ai/agent-s.

articles.title: Neural Implicit Energy Optimization for LiDAR Mapping
articles.content: Neural implicit representations provide memory-efficient signed distance field (SDF) parameterizations for large-scale LiDAR scenes, but the geometry recovered from sparse and often noisy inputs carries jitter and artifacts. Classical geometric optimization techniques resolve such artifacts with surface energy functionals, whose minimizers correspond to smooth surfaces. Motivated by this principle, we formulate neural LiDAR mapping as the optimization of energy functionals over the parameter space of neural implicit representations. Specifically, we regularize the signed distance field with an energy functional defined on the shape operator of its level set, which represents the curvature of the surface, thus encouraging smoothness along the surface. This adapts classical geometric priors to the scale of million-point LiDAR maps. Experiments on large-scale datasets show reconstructions with improved smoothness at preserved geometric fidelity, and no additional inference-time cost. The code is publicly available at \href{https://github.com/HrishikeshVish/nieo}{https://github.com/HrishikeshVish/nieo}

articles.title: What Do RTL Repair Benchmarks Actually Measure?
articles.content: RTL repair benchmarks should measure whether a model can fix broken RTL given a specification. To this end, we construct and hash-bind RTLRepairDataset, 5,784 (broken, fixed) training pairs; RTLRepairBench, 459 held-out cases with 374 syntactic and 85 behavioral mutations; and an evaluation harness supporting simulation and formal equivalence. We then use this infrastructure to identify two measurement confounds. First, simulation and formal scoring give opposite signs for the apparent effect of providing a specification in one evaluated cohort; reset-aware rescoring attributes almost all of the simulation-formal disagreement to reset and first-cycle comparison semantics. Second, on 274 mined model failures, the specification-only minus specification-conditioned recovery point estimate ranges from -8.5 to +18.3 percentage points across six models. Thus, a conventional repair score need not isolate whether the model used the faulty RTL. We translate these findings into evaluation controls: report initialization, reset, first-cycle, and unknown-value semantics; disclose oracle coverage and undecided cases; and include a specification-only baseline. Together, the resources and audit provide both a benchmark for behavioral repair and a protocol for diagnosing what contributes to its measured score. We release the benchmark, the training set, construction code, sanitized aggregate evidence, and reproduction materials at https://github.com/Evaaaz/RTLRepairBench.

articles.title: Learning the 4D World through Point Trajectory Forecasting
articles.content: Reliable multi-view forecasting requires videos from different cameras to describe the same evolving 3D scene. To this end, we introduce Video-Point Model (VPM), a world model that conditions on multi-view video histories and a language instruction to jointly forecast future videos from arbitrary viewpoints and the 3D trajectories of persistent scene points. We extend a pretrained world model with camera-conditioned multi-view processing that integrates complementary observations across cameras, and add a trajectory head that predicts how physical points move through time. Each trajectory tracks a single point across all views, and supervising these trajectories alongside video generation therefore anchors appearance changes in every camera to a shared description of 3D motion. To support training and evaluation, we build VPM-Data, a simulation corpus pairing synchronized multi-view videos with persistent point trajectories, and VP-WorldBench, a forecasting benchmark spanning simulated and real environments. We further extend VPM to robot control by adding robot actions as a token modality in the generator. Action tokens share the point-supervised backbone and are denoised jointly with future videos, thereby grounding the policy in the same 3D-aware representation. On VP-WorldBench and existing 4D generation benchmarks, point supervision improves both video fidelity and 3D motion accuracy over a video-only counterpart, and in simulated and real-robot experiments, it also raises the manipulation success of the action-enabled model.

articles.title: PaPi: Parallel Picard-Duhamel Integration for Fast Neuro-Spectral Architectures
articles.content: Neuro-spectral architectures (NeuSA) are a class of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) that have proven effective for solving time-dependent PDEs in the frequency domain. However, training and inference often rely on costly numerical integration of the learned vector field, typically using sequential Runge-Kutta time stepping, which limits temporal parallelism. We introduce PaPi, an integration scheme inspired by weakly nonlinear flows that enables time-Parallel inference through exponential integration and a Duhamel-Picard scheme. We show that the Duhamel-Picard iteration converges exponentially for all flows, and provide explicit error bounds that depend on how close the flow is to linear. Experiments show that PaPi accelerates training and inference by up to two orders of magnitude, achieving training times of under one second for low-dimensional PDE learning problems, while maintaining competitive predictive accuracy.

articles.title: WildMAE: Structure-Aware Masked Autoencoding for Wildlife Image Reconstruction
articles.content: Camera-trap imagery presents substantial variation in animal appearance, illumination, background clutter, and visual degradation. Masked autoencoders (MAEs) offer a label-free framework for modeling such data through reconstruction of randomly hidden image patches. We present WildMAE, a decoder-side extension of MAE that combines local structure-aware refinement with masked-to-visible cross-attention. A zero-gated convolutional residual path introduces a two-dimensional neighborhood prior, while gated cross-attention allows masked positions to retrieve contextual information from visible-position features without replacing the original Transformer decoder. The associated training recipe progressively introduces normalized-pixel, Sobel-edge, and perceptual objectives. In the original Snapshot Serengeti study, covering 4,744 test images at 75% masking, the reported reconstruction scores were 27.90 versus 24.33 dB PSNR, 0.840 versus 0.780 SSIM, and 0.160 versus 0.320 LPIPS for WildMAE and vanilla MAE, respectively. Additional historical records document favorable average differences under four synthetic degradation conditions and describe component variants. We present the method, experimental observations, and their scope together: the retained metrics are historical protocol-dependent results, rather than a newly reproduced, harmonized comparison or a validation of restoration from genuinely unavailable pixels. WildMAE provides a practical architectural case study for combining global token mixing with spatial and targeted contextual refinement in wildlife masked-image modeling.

articles.title: AgenticRoboRL: Bringing Coding-Agent Post-Training to Agentic Robotics
articles.content: Agentic robotics systems combine planners with robot harnesses to perform complex manipulation tasks. Recent work improves these systems through better harnesses and external memory, but relies on powerful closed-source models as planners and does not improve the planners' own capabilities. In contrast, coding agents have improved substantially by post-training the model itself. We therefore investigate whether post-training can also improve robot planners. However, applying it across robot harnesses requires accommodating different execution mechanisms, including VLA skill invocation and control-code generation. To this end, we introduce AgenticRoboRL, a framework for post-training robot planners across different harnesses. The training recipe combines supervised fine-tuning with multi-turn reinforcement learning. To accommodate different execution mechanisms, harness-specific adapters connect recorded planner interactions with task outcomes, enabling a common RL training pipeline while keeping execution components fixed. On LIBERO-PRO, AgenticRoboRL raises the success rate of a 9B-parameter planner from 18.1% to 71.0% without external memory, approaching the 72.1% achieved by Codex (GPT-5.5) with external memory. These results demonstrate post-training as an effective approach for improving robot planners. We will release the framework and trained planner checkpoints.

articles.title: Capable Teacher, Myopic Scorer: Reward-Free Teacher Repair for Agentic On-Policy Distillation
articles.content: Agentic on-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student agent on its own trajectories while a teacher scores every token. A natural explanation of where it goes wrong is compounding error: the student's mistakes carry its trajectories beyond the region where the teacher is reliable, so recent methods keep training inside that region, through episode-length curricula, teacher-guided turns, prefix replay, or teacher intervention where the two disagree. We show this explanation is incomplete. From the states where the student departs most from the teacher, the teacher's own takeovers still finish the task, yet the student trained on its token scores keeps running out of turns. We attribute this to the myopia of next-token scoring. The teacher rates each token without seeing where the episode ends, so its scores let through the safe, delaying moves that outcome-based RL would punish with zero reward, a penalty agentic OPD lacks. We call this difference between what the teacher does and what it scores the rollout-scorer gap. We propose Rollout-to-Scorer Distillation (R2S), which repairs the scorer before distillation by mining high-disagreement states from the untrained student, running teacher takeovers from them, keeping the states where enough takeovers pass a reward-free check such as consensus or an LLM judge, and fine-tuning the teacher to give its takeover-informed scores on every assistant token from the divergence turn onward, without the takeover in context. The repaired teacher is frozen as the sole scorer for standard OPD, requiring no task reward during repair or training. Across three environments, two teachers and four students, R2S outperforms three state-of-the-art agentic-OPD methods in all twelve teacher-student-environment cells, by 12.8 success points on average over the best of them in each cell. Project page: https://tree-shu-zhao.github.io/r2s/.

articles.title: SceneRig: An Agentic System for Simulation-Ready 3D Scene Reconstruction from Single Images
articles.content: Simulation is a powerful tool for robotics, but building diverse, simulation-ready scenes at scale remains difficult. Reconstructing scenes from single images is a promising alternative, but visual similarity alone is insufficient: objects must also be recovered, accurately placed, and physically grounded. Existing methods that rely on post-hoc physics settling often misplace objects, producing scenes that look correct but behave poorly under manipulation. We present SceneRig, an agentic system that turns a single image into an editable, simulation-ready scene. SceneRig combines geometric, visual, and physical tools to reconstruct a faithful 3D scene. An agent then performs edit-and-validate loops inside a physics simulator to achieve physical stability. Across diverse inputs, SceneRig improves instance segmentation, object-centric appearance, and 3D placement while keeping the reconstructed scenes physically stable. Furthermore, SceneRig is effective for downstream robotics: its scenes predict real-robot policy outcomes more accurately than the baseline method and more reliably support replay of recorded manipulations without trajectory adaptation.

articles.title: Beyond the Sequentiality Bottleneck: A Hybrid Diffusion-Autoregressive Framework for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning
articles.content: Autoregressive models (ARMs) face a "Sequentiality Bottleneck" in reasoning, while diffusion language models (DLMs) offer parallelism but lack semantic coherence. To addresses both limitations, we propose Collaborative Reasoning Asymmetric Learning (CoRAL), a hybrid framework via an Asymmetric Planner-Executor (APE) architecture: a DLM Planner generates K diverse reasoning trajectories in parallel, while a large ARM Executor selects the optimal plan and synthesizes the final answer. To train the Planner effectively, we introduce Reward-Guided Denoising for CoT (RDC), which integrates outcome-based rewards into the diffusion process to steer it toward goal-directed reasoning. Experiments on vision-language benchmarks show that CoRAL significantly outperforms prior diffusion-based methods and achieves competitive performance against strong ARMs, achieving both superior efficiency and quality.

articles.title: 启元机器人新进展：北大董豪团队推出 HIL-UMI，让后训练摆脱「真机依赖」
articles.content: 继无本体之后，具身后训练范式有了新进展。    作者丨齐铖湧    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       最近，具身行业讨论“无本体进行后训练的可能性”的热度很高。国内外目前还没有团队做出可行方案。说白了，无论是大模型还是具身机器人，想真正好用，光靠预训练打基础可不行，最终落地全靠“后训练”来调教。启元机器人首席科学家董豪告诉AI科技评论：“预训练提升的是下限，上限还得看后训练。”当前具身公司追求进厂打工、家庭保洁等真实落地，比的就是成功率，也就是在比拼后训练的实力。可后训练，难就难在它得跟真实物理世界打交道，过去都得用纯真机数据。但真机训练成本太高，要大规模铺开，那么多的机器人本体，硬件磨损、场地、人工都是天价。所以，行业内预训练已经开始转向用“无本体”设备采集数据，虽然量上去了，但传统后训练最关键的“纠错”环节却没法搞定。为了解决这个行业难题，北大和启元机器人董豪团队推出了HIL-UMI。这个工作，围绕着具身后训练阶段无本体的前提下，围绕着最关键的“纠错”环节展开。论文地址：https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.20659项目主页：https://hil-umi.github.io01具身后训练的成本，为何远超大模型RLHF？跟大模型比起来，具身行业的后训练太贵，是很多具身模型无法尝试Scaling的重要原因。大语言模型能变得这么好用，大家心里都清楚：不光是预训练数据量大，更关键的是后面有RLHF（人类反馈强化学习，可以简单理解为数据标注）和DPO这些“后训练”的功劳。但具身机器人的后训练，成本可比大模型的RLHF高出不止百倍。大模型做RLHF，无非是请更多人坐在电脑前点点选选；可具身机器人，那就得真刀真枪地跟物理世界打交道。拿传统上最常用的DAgger，也就是用人类或者算法作为专家评价后训练的模式，这套流程虽然有效，但又贵又慢。比较常见的，是以传统的真机人在回路（也就是 HG-DAgger：Human-Gated DAgger），机械臂在运作，人类操作员坐在旁边高度紧张地盯着，等它快抓空、快撞车的时候紧急接管，把正确的轨迹录下来，这就是人类来把关整个训练回路。最麻烦的是，每次校正完，还得人工把被碰乱的现场恢复原样。等机器人执行，人工干预，环境复位，一坐一下午，能用的数据不多。这其中绝大部分时间，都耗在机器人的笨拙动作和人工环境复位上。这种又慢又烧钱的模式，让后训练数据规模采集成了个老大难，严重限制了规模化。这就引出了一个核心问题：我们能不能摆脱真机，就像平时做家务一样，顺手就把模型最需要的“纠错”数据给采集了？02HIL-UMI 的底层逻辑：给UMI 采集加了一个“模型大脑”HIL-UMI 的做法非常聪明，概括起来就是一句话：“不用机器人，也能给机器人补课。”HIL-UMI ，指的是Human-In-the-Loop（人在环路）UMI，和过去大家常用 UMI（手持夹爪）采集数据不同，HIL-UMI 的采集，不是“盲目”的，而是加入了一个模型。HIL-UMI 把模型直接接进了这个手持采集过程：真实世界里只有人在动： 操作员手里拿着 UMI 夹爪正常干活（比如抓玩具、叠毛巾），摄像头同步拍摄画面。模型在后台“脑补”： 模型接收着相同的画面和任务指令，在后台快速预测“如果换我来，接下来的 20 步动作该怎么做”，但它并不真正控制任何机械臂。发现分歧立刻触发提示： 系统在后台实时比对人类实际动作与模型预测动作。如果两者差不多，说明模型已经掌握，不需要重复录；一旦发现模型“脑补”的轨迹跟人类的真实操作严重跑偏（说明模型在这个场景下是个“生手”），系统就会立刻提示操作者：“这一段模型不会，从这里开始多教一段！”手持夹爪与采集设备整个过程，不需要机械臂在场，更不需要机器人真去犯一次错。人类在示范的同时，就把模型在真实部署中极可能翻车的场景给定点捕获了。03不是数采集工具，是后训练

articles.title: Git 被换掉，LLM 被替代：AI 编码开始反噬传统工具链？
articles.content: Anthropic 代码量暴涨，GitHub 密钥扫描又慢又贵，两家被迫改造系统。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       Git 已经支撑软件开发二十多年，Anthropic 却决定把它换掉。为了让 Claude 持续生成的代码顺利进入开发流程，7 名工程师花了 5 个月，开发出版本控制系统 Scion，并将核心代码仓库迁移过去。今年 5 月，Anthropic 每天平均合并约 2500 项代码变更，到 9 月已超过 3 万项，仅 CI 系统每天就要执行约 2500 万次代码检出。写代码的速度上来了，准备仓库、同步对象和查询历史却越来越费机器。几乎同一时期，GitHub 用微调后的 ModernBERT 替换密钥扫描中的通用 LLM 判断。哥伦比亚大学与 Google DeepMind 等机构则通过 BTTF，把芯片仿真波形转换成 SQLite，让 Agent 使用 SQL 排查异常。Scion 默认在线，BTTF 将波形变成查询接口，GitHub 把高频判断交给分类器。围绕人类开发节奏设计的系统，开始承受 Agent 带来的另一种负载。01Git 的离线能力，为什么成了负担Git 的分布式设计让工程师克隆仓库后，即使断网也能提交、合并、查看历史。但 Anthropic 大量读取代码的任务是始终联网的 CI 作业和 Agent 沙箱，运行几分钟便销毁，可能只需要几个文件、一份 diff，或确认两个提交的祖先关系。为了这些操作准备本地仓库，重复成本越来越高。Anthropic 主分支历史接近 100 GB，压缩工作副本超过 25 GB。若每天 2500 万次检出分别获取完整副本，理论流量会超过 600 PB。公司虽用浅克隆、稀疏检出、快照和数百台 Git 镜像，但镜像仍要同步、快照会过期，历史查询还需补齐对象。仓库越活跃，维护成本越高。Scion 将客户端缩成轻量入口。提交创建、合并、变基与历史查询放到中心服务，本地仅监测文件变化、维护少量缓存，需要工作目录时按需展开。CI 若只想计算 diff，可以直接调用 API，无须完整检出。这牺牲了离线自治，却减少重复初始化。提交格式也变了。Git commit 指向描述仓库状态的目录树，Scion 的 changeset 则以预写日志条目记录相对首个父提交修改过的文件，通过内容寻址指针引用数据。创建 changeset 无须生成 Git packfile，也不用立即移动共享分支，只有 main 等引用更新时，系统才对 Spanner 中的单行记录执行 compare-and-swap。Agent 可以并发生成变更，竞争集中到分支引用移动时。但历史查询仍有难题：增量记录无法直接回答某行是谁改的、文件经历过什么。Scion 为 blame、路径历史与提交图跳表维护 derived data，按父提交关系预计算，或等查询发生后再生成。写入与历史分析可以独立扩展。雷峰网检出时，scn 客户端从目标目录树开始，只请求缺失的 tree 和 blob。请求依次经过节点上的 scion-daemon、区域 scion-cache，再由 scion-server 回源到 Spanner 或对象存储。对象写入后不可变，缓存能够跨任务复用，减少协商、压缩及反复传输。Anthropic 称缓存命中率超过 99%，并限制故障时的回源流量。迁移后，Scion 相较旧 Git 镜像体系的 CPU 和内存需求约缩小 200 倍，检出从分钟级降至秒级，CI 释放约 25% 的 CPU 容量。200 倍说的是基础设施资源占用，并非 Git 操作整体提速。Anthropic 还同步建设 Antique 代码评审、源码搜索、IAM 和批量合并工具，以适配新协议。在线服务的维护也成了新成本。02让数据库读波形，Agent 才能追查故障芯片验证面对的是另一种障碍。

articles.title: Muse Wonder 建模大翻车，亚历山大·王辩护遭马斯克无情补刀
articles.content: 官方承认 3D 短板，跨模型测试 Harness 不同。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       Meta 刚发布的 Muse Wonder，没想到因为一盏熔岩灯，在开发者社区引发了一场关于 AI 模型跑分的争论。10 月 12 日，Meta 推出 Muse Wonder 和 Muse Wonder Full，主打 Coding Agent、工具调用和长任务执行能力。官方公布的成绩相当亮眼，Wonder Full 在 SWE-Marathon 上拿到 57.5 分，DeepSWE 1.1 达到 79.0 分，已经能够与同期的前沿模型展开竞争。然而，开发者社区 BridgeMind 随后安排了一项 3D 编程测试，要求 Muse Wonder 制作一盏具有透明玻璃外壳、动态熔岩和光照效果的熔岩灯。结果模型只生成了一个红色圆柱体。BridgeMind 随即质疑 Muse Wonder 存在严重的 Benchmaxxing，也就是针对 Benchmark 进行大量优化，成绩看着漂亮，碰上陌生任务却露了怯。连马斯克也忍不住下场，在相关帖子下意味深长地回了一句 Hmm。短短一个词，虽然没有明确表态，却让这场围绕 Meta 新模型的刷分争议又添了几分戏剧性。Meta 首席 AI 官 Alexandr Wang 很快回应，团队确实没有针对 3D 演示游戏进行显式训练，事后看来或许应该补充相关训练，但他仍然希望开发者实际体验 Muse Wonder 的 Coding 能力。雷峰网这场争论有一个重要前提：熔岩灯测试针对的是普通版 Muse Wonder，而 Meta 公布的部分突出成绩来自 Wonder Full，两者存在能力差异。同时，Meta 官方 Model Card 已经明确承认，视觉与空间推理，尤其是 3D 任务，属于 Muse Wonder 的已知短板。但高分模型在陌生任务中遭遇如此明显的失败，依然让人好奇：当前大模型的训练方法究竟在强化哪些能力，Agent Benchmark 又能在多大程度上反映模型的实际水平？01奖励机制，决定模型擅长解决什么问题Muse Wonder 的表现，与当前大模型越来越依赖 Post-training 提升任务能力的技术路线有关。在 Pre-training 阶段，模型通过大规模数据学习语言、代码、空间关系和其他通用知识。进入 Post-training 后，训练会进一步塑造模型的行为策略，尤其是通过强化学习，让它在特定任务环境中形成更稳定的执行能力。Coding Agent 很适合这类训练。例如，给模型一个存在 Bug 的代码仓库，要求它定位问题、修改文件并运行测试。整个过程可以通过编译结果、单元测试和功能检查获得相对明确的反馈。强化学习系统据此判断哪些操作有效，持续强化能够提高任务成功率的行为。训练规模扩大后，模型逐渐学会一套复杂的软件工程策略，包括如何缩小搜索范围、选择工具、处理报错，以及在多轮修改中维护任务状态。Meta 在官方技术文章中提到，Muse Wonder 接受了多样化长任务训练，并引入 Active Focus，使模型能够在遭遇阻碍后尝试其他方案、恢复执行并继续推进任务。但这类训练依赖一个关键条件：环境必须能够向模型提供有用的反馈。熔岩灯恰好打破了传统 Coding Agent 熟悉的反馈方式。雷峰网从程序实现来看，熔岩灯涉及三维几何、透明材质、光照计算和动态形变。如果使用 Three.js，模型需要构造玻璃灯罩，为内部熔岩生成不规则的几何形态，再通过时间变量或噪声函数驱动形状变化。这些代码即使能够正常执行，画面仍然可能完全错误。例如，透明材质的参数配置不当，玻璃就可能变成不透明的实体，熔岩形状缺少连续变化机制，内部效果就可能退化为静态色块。编译器和单元测试很难直接判断这些视觉问题。这意味着，Agent 还需要具备一套
